explanation: The correct answer is C (That the open layout will be too noisy to work in.): Jenna says she worked in an open office before and it got really noisy, especially near the printer area. Option A is wrong because Jenna never mentions the number of phone booths as a problem. Option B is wrong because no delay to the move is discussed. Option D is wrong because distance from the printer is not her stated concern, noise is.
transcript:
Sam: Have you seen the new floor plan they posted for our office renovation? They're getting rid of all the cubicles.
Jenna: Yeah, I saw it. I'm honestly not thrilled. I like having some walls around my desk when I'm on calls.
Sam: I get that, but they're adding those small phone booths for private calls. I think the open layout might actually help our team collaborate more.
Jenna: Maybe, but I've worked in an open office before and it got really noisy, especially near the printer area.
Sam: Fair point. I guess we'll just have to see how it goes once we move in next month.

question: What part of the proposal changes Tom's opinion by the end of the conversation?

options.A: The city agreeing to clear the weeds before construction begins.
options.B: The inclusion of a volunteer schedule and a watering budget.
options.C: A promise that the lot will be fenced off from the street.
options.D: The city offering free seeds to every household nearby.

explanation: The correct answer is B (The inclusion of a volunteer schedule and a watering budget.): Rina explains the proposal includes a volunteer schedule and a small watering budget from the city, and Tom says this makes him feel better about supporting it. Option A is wrong because clearing weeds beforehand is not mentioned. Option C is wrong because fencing is never discussed in the conversation. Option D is wrong because free seeds are not part of what changes Tom's mind.
transcript:
Tom: Did you hear the city is thinking about turning that empty lot on Elm Street into a community garden?
Rina: I did, and I think it's a great idea. That lot has just been sitting there collecting weeds for years.
Tom: I agree it looks bad, but I'm a bit worried about who's going to maintain it once the novelty wears off.
Rina: That's fair, but the proposal actually includes a volunteer schedule and a small watering budget from the city.
Tom: Oh, I didn't know that part. That actually makes me feel a lot better about supporting it.

question: What is Alisha's view on the new dress code policy?

options.A: She thinks the policy should be cancelled and reconsidered again next quarter.
options.B: She believes jeans should rarely be allowed in the office except on Fridays.
options.C: She wants the relaxed dress code limited to just Mondays instead of Fridays.
options.D: She is comfortable starting small and possibly expanding it later.

explanation: The correct answer is D (She is comfortable starting small and possibly expanding it later.): Alisha says she doesn't mind starting small and that maybe they'll extend it to the whole week later if it goes well. Option A is wrong because Alisha supports the policy rather than wanting it cancelled. Option B is wrong because she is glad jeans are now allowed on Fridays. Option C is wrong because Fridays, not Mondays, are the day mentioned in the conversation.
transcript:
Kevin: Did you read the email about the updated dress code? They're loosening it up for Fridays.
Alisha: I saw that. Jeans and sneakers are finally allowed, at least on Fridays.
Kevin: Honestly I think they should just allow it every day. I don't see why Friday is any different from Monday.
Alisha: I actually don't mind starting small. If it goes well, maybe they'll extend it to the whole week later.
Kevin: That's a more patient way to look at it than I was, I suppose.

question: What does Devon believe is the likely cause of the higher hydro bill?

options.A: The space heater he has been using often in his room.
options.B: A billing error made by the hydro company itself.
options.C: Maya leaving the kitchen lights on overnight repeatedly.
options.D: A new appliance that was installed earlier in the month.

explanation: The correct answer is A (The space heater he has been using often in his room.): Devon says he thinks it might be the space heater in his room since he has been using it a lot since it got colder. Option B is wrong because no billing error is suggested in the conversation. Option C is wrong because kitchen lights are never mentioned. Option D is wrong because no new appliance is discussed as the cause.
transcript:
Devon: I was looking at last month's hydro bill and it's almost double what we usually pay.
Maya: Really? That seems high. Did we leave something running by accident?
Devon: I think it might be the space heater in my room. I've been using it a lot since it got colder.
Maya: That would explain it. Maybe we should split the extra cost this month since it benefits both of us staying warm.
Devon: That sounds fair to me, I'll cover a bit more next time if I keep using it.

question: What is Omar initially worried about regarding the four day work week?

options.A: That his salary would be reduced along with the shorter week.
options.B: That the same amount of work would be crammed into fewer days.
options.C: That the pilot program would only apply to certain departments.
options.D: That customers would be unhappy with reduced office hours.

explanation: The correct answer is B (That the same amount of work would be crammed into fewer days.): Omar directly asks whether they would just end up cramming the same work into fewer days. Option A is wrong because salary is never mentioned in the conversation. Option C is wrong because department limits are not discussed. Option D is wrong because customer reaction is not part of Omar's stated worry.
transcript:
Layla: Our manager mentioned the company might try a four day work week next quarter.
Omar: I heard that too. I'm a little skeptical, honestly. Won't we just end up cramming the same work into fewer days?
Layla: That's a valid worry, but the pilot program apparently reduces total workload too, not just the schedule.
Omar: Oh, if the workload actually goes down, that changes things. I was picturing the same deadlines with less time.
Layla: Exactly, that's why I'm cautiously optimistic about giving it a try.

question: According to Priya, what is one advantage of switching to the gym near her apartment?

options.A: It offers a lower monthly membership fee than downtown.
options.B: It has personal trainers included at no extra cost.
options.C: It is farther from her apartment but has better equipment.
options.D: It is closer to home, which would save her commuting time.

explanation: The correct answer is D (It is closer to home, which would save her commuting time.): Priya says the new gym is actually closer to home than the downtown one, so it would save her time overall. Option A is wrong because membership fees are never discussed. Option B is wrong because personal trainers are not mentioned in the conversation. Option C is wrong because Priya explicitly says it is closer, not farther, from her apartment.
transcript:
Priya: I'm thinking about switching gyms. The one downtown is way more crowded than when I first joined.
Ethan: I've noticed that too when I've gone with you. What's pulling you toward a different one?
Priya: There's a new gym near my apartment with a pool and way shorter lines for equipment.
Ethan: That does sound nice, but isn't it a longer commute for you after work?
Priya: Actually no, it's closer to home than the downtown one, so it would save me time overall.

question: According to Grace, where is the shipping delay actually happening?

options.A: At the client's own receiving warehouse location.
options.B: Somewhere within their company's internal shipping department.
options.C: At the shipping company's sorting facility during transit.
options.D: During the final delivery step by the local courier driver.

explanation: The correct answer is C (At the shipping company's sorting facility during transit.): Grace says the tracking logs show the delay is happening at the shipping company's sorting facility, not on their own end. Option A is wrong because the client's warehouse is not mentioned as the cause. Option B is wrong because Grace specifically clears their own company's warehouse of blame. Option D is wrong because the local courier driver is never mentioned in the conversation.
transcript:
Noah: Did you see the complaint that came in from the Whitmore account this morning?
Grace: I did. They're upset the shipment arrived three days late again.
Noah: I figured it was something like that. Do you think it's our warehouse or the shipping company causing the delays?
Grace: Honestly, I checked the tracking logs, and it looks like the delay is happening at the shipping company's sorting facility, not on our end.
Noah: That's good to know, at least we can show the client it wasn't our warehouse dropping the ball.

question: Why does the new pickup time create a problem for Farah specifically?

options.A: Her work schedule does not end early enough to make the new time.
options.B: She does not have a car available on most days during the school week.
options.C: The school recently changed the pickup location to a much farther entrance gate.
options.D: Carlos is unable to help her with pickup most days during the week.

explanation: The correct answer is A (Her work schedule does not end early enough to make the new time.): Farah says the new time is going to be tough for her since she does not get off work until right around that time. Option B is wrong because a lack of a car is never mentioned. Option C is wrong because the pickup location is not discussed, only the time. Option D is wrong because Carlos actually offers to help her on the difficult days.
transcript:
Farah: Did you get the note from the school about the new pickup time?
Carlos: Yeah, they're moving it up by fifteen minutes starting next week.
Farah: That's going to be tough for me since I don't get off work until right around that new time.
Carlos: I could probably pick up both our kids on the days it's hard for you, if that would help.
Farah: That would honestly be a huge help, thank you for offering.

question: Which speaker believes the best approach depends on the type of task being done?

options.A: Deb, since she focuses only on saving commuting time.
options.B: Marcus, since he believes teamwork often suffers when everyone works remotely.
options.C: All three speakers agree that working from home is worse.
options.D: Yuki, since she says it depends on the day and the task.

explanation: The correct answer is D (Yuki, since she says it depends on the day and the task.): Yuki says it depends on the day, explaining that some tasks need quiet focus at home while meetings work better in person. Option A is wrong because Deb talks about commuting time, not task-dependent preference. Option B is wrong because Marcus expresses a firm dislike of remote work rather than a task-based view. Option C is wrong because the speakers do not all agree, Deb clearly supports working from home.
transcript:
Interviewer: We asked people downtown what they think about companies allowing permanent work from home. Here's what they said.
Speaker 1, Deb: I love it. I save two hours a day not commuting, and I'm actually more productive at my kitchen table.
Speaker 2, Marcus: I disagree completely. I miss the energy of being around coworkers, and I think teamwork suffers when everyone's scattered.
Speaker 3, Yuki: For me it depends on the day. Some tasks need quiet focus at home, but meetings really work better in person.

question: Which speaker's main objection is about the impact on farmland?

options.A: Hassan, because he is mainly worried about pedestrian safety in the downtown core.
options.B: Colette, because she says it would cut through local family farmland.
options.C: Ben, because he mentions the new wildlife crossing included in the proposed plan.
options.D: None of the speakers mention farmland anywhere in their comments during the discussion.

explanation: The correct answer is B (Colette, because she says it would cut through local family farmland.): Colette says she is against the bypass because it would cut right through farmland that's been in local families for generations. Option A is wrong because Hassan actually supports the bypass for pedestrian safety reasons. Option C is wrong because Ben's comment is about a wildlife crossing, not farmland. Option D is wrong because Colette clearly raises the farmland concern.
transcript:
Interviewer: The city is debating a new highway bypass around town. We asked three residents for their thoughts.
Speaker 1, Hassan: I'm all for it. Right now trucks go straight through downtown, and it's loud and dangerous for pedestrians.
Speaker 2, Colette: I'm against it, honestly. That bypass would cut right through farmland that's been in local families for generations.
Speaker 3, Ben: I haven't fully decided, but I do like that the plan includes a wildlife crossing to protect local deer populations.

question: Which speaker believes the new pet fee is unfair because of an existing deposit?

options.A: Nadia, because she says tenants already pay a pet deposit.
options.B: Owen, because he thinks pets cause wear and tear.
options.C: Ingrid, because she is only concerned about the exact amount.
options.D: All three speakers agree the fee is somewhat unfair overall.

explanation: The correct answer is A (Nadia, because she says tenants already pay a pet deposit.): Nadia says the fee feels unfair since tenants already pay a pet deposit, calling the new charge double charging. Option B is wrong because Owen actually supports the fee due to wear and tear concerns. Option C is wrong because Ingrid's concern is about the amount, not the existing deposit. Option D is wrong because Owen and Ingrid do not both call it completely unfair.
transcript:
Interviewer: A local property company wants to add a monthly pet fee for tenants with animals. Here's what tenants told us.
Speaker 1, Nadia: I think it's unfair. We already pay a pet deposit, so an extra monthly fee feels like double charging.
Speaker 2, Owen: I actually understand it. Pets can cause wear and tear on carpets and floors, so a small fee seems reasonable to me.
Speaker 3, Ingrid: My concern is more about the amount. If it stays low, I won't mind, but I've heard some buildings charge way too much.

question: Which speaker points out that current ridership numbers are lower than expected?

options.A: Fiona, because she is focused on her own commute time.
options.B: Priya, because she talks about the suburbs growing quickly.
options.C: Darnell, because he questions whether the cost is worth it.
options.D: None of the speakers mention ridership numbers during the conversation.

explanation: The correct answer is C (Darnell, because he questions whether the cost is worth it.): Darnell says he is not convinced it's worth the cost because ridership numbers on the current line are already lower than expected. Option A is wrong because Fiona's comment focuses on her own commute time, not ridership. Option B is wrong because Priya discusses suburban growth rather than current ridership figures. Option D is wrong because Darnell clearly raises the ridership point.
transcript:
Interviewer: The city is considering extending the LRT line further into the suburbs. We spoke to three commuters.
Speaker 1, Fiona: I'm excited about it. It would cut my commute time in half once it reaches my neighbourhood.
Speaker 2, Darnell: I'm not convinced it's worth the cost. Ridership numbers on the current line are already lower than expected.
Speaker 3, Priya: I think it's a good long term investment, even if ridership is low right now, because the suburbs are still growing quickly.

question: Which speaker raises a concern about the upfront cost of uniforms specifically?

options.A: Wendy, because she says uniforms would save money overall.
options.B: Amir, because he focuses on self expression through clothing.
options.C: Both Wendy and Amir mention cost as their main concern.
options.D: Sonia, because she worries uniforms might cost more upfront.

explanation: The correct answer is D (Sonia, because she worries uniforms might cost more upfront.): Sonia says she worries uniforms might actually cost more upfront than regular clothes.
